events.region: Waters from Pt. Sal to Santa Cruz Island CA and westward 60 nm including San Miguel and Santa Rosa Islands; Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente Island to 60 NM offshore including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and
combined seas 8 to 13 ft possible when conditions are worst.

* WHERE...Waters from Pt. Sal to Santa Cruz Island CA and
westward 60 nm including San Miguel and Santa Rosa Islands and
Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente Island to
60 NM offshore including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 6 PM PDT Saturday.
For the Gale Watch, from Saturday evening through Monday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Potentially strong winds may create dangerous sea
conditions which could capsize or damage small and large
vessels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...See the Coastal Waters Forecast (CWFLOX)
for more.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound; Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out 20 NM; Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to 60 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
For the following areas...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to 60
NM...

At 602 AM CDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts
were located along a line extending from near Navarre Beach to near
Oriskany Reef, moving north at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Mary Esther, East Santa Rosa Sound, Okaloosa Pier, Oriskany Reef,
Fort Walton Liberty Ship Reef, and Navarre Beach.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Harrison, IN; Perry, IN; Breckinridge, KY; Hancock, KY; Meade, KY
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Harrison County in south central Indiana...
Southern Perry County in south central Indiana...
Central Breckinridge County in central Kentucky...
Hancock County in central Kentucky...
Meade County in central Kentucky...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM EDT /900 AM CDT/.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 701 AM EDT /601 AM CDT/, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain
due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tell City, Brandenburg, Hardinsburg, Hawesville, Webster,
Lewisport, Cannelton, Irvington, Cloverport and Muldraugh.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...

* Until 700 AM CDT.

* At 559 AM CDT, strong thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from near
Blackwater Bay Bridge to 8 nm southeast of Pensacola Beach, moving
northeast at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Navarre Beach, West Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Beach, Escambia Bay
Bridge, Blackwater Bay Bridge, East Bay, Escambia Bay, Pensacola
Bay Bridge, and Garcon Point Bridge.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Chesapeake Bay from Pooles Island to Sandy Point MD; Chesapeake Bay from Sandy Point to North Beach MD; Chesapeake Bay from North Beach to Drum Point MD; Chesapeake Bay from Drum Point MD to Smith Point VA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Recent buoy observations have indicated gusts have begun to
approach 20 knots over the upper and middle portions of the
Chesapeake Bay. This will likely continue, particularly as rain
showers track in from the I-95 corridor. These elevated gusts
could persist another couple of hours.

Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating small craft,
should exercise extra caution or consider altering navigating
plans due to these conditions.

events.region: Muscatine; Scott; Louisa; Des Moines; Rock Island; Henry; Bureau; Putnam; Mercer
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Dense fog is developing early this morning, reducing visibility
below a quarter of a mile at times. There are areas where the fog
is limited or not as thick, so if you are traveling be prepared
for rapid changes in visibility. If you encounter fog, remember
to slow down, use your low beams, and allow extra distance between
you and other vehicles.
